documents.title: Artificial Intelligence at Tulane University: Guidelines for the Ethical and Responsible Use of AI
documents.stance_why: The page sets no student rule of its own: it says student use is 'already covered in our academic integrity policies' and that 'Each instructor has the option of putting in place guidelines' for their course. Faculty are told 'Rather than restricting AI' to explore it. Decision handed to instructors, so delegates.
documents.summary: University AI page that frames AI as an opportunity and points student questions to existing integrity policies. It sets data-protection and security-review rules, leaves course rules to instructors with a clear-instructions requirement, and promises workshops and policy revision.

units.why: The opening states the university's purpose for AI: it 'recognizes the potential' of AI. This is a framing statement of principle, so P56 (institution-level framework/preamble), informs, general.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: actor=all, phase=general, modality=informs, policy_type=P56, unit_stance=neutral. Coder B: actor=all, phase=general, modality=informs, policy_type=P87, unit_stance=neutral. Resolution: Coder A coded P56 (institution-level framework), B coded P87 (benefits of AI for learning). The sentence says the university 'recognizes the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to reshape the educational and research landscape'; it frames the whole document and names no learning benefit, so P56 stands. Final: actor=all, phase=general, modality=informs, policy_type=P56, unit_stance=neutral.
units.anchor: recognizes the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to reshape the educational and research landscape

units.why: States the guiding principle: reap AI's benefits 'while preserving the intellectual integrity and human-centered model'. A principle for the whole institution, so P56 rather than P87 (benefits only) since it balances benefit and integrity.
units.anchor: reap its benefits while preserving the intellectual integrity and human-centered model of our university

units.uncovered_note: The university states its investment in AI research centers and its aim of leadership in AI research and application.

units.why: The provost 'established two committees' to learn about campus needs, which states who shaped the guidance, so P84; not P80 since the committees advise rather than enforce.

units.why: Student AI use is governed by existing integrity policies rather than a new AI rule: 'already covered in our academic integrity policies'. This is P77 (follow existing university policy); P36 would need explicit mention of misconduct classification, which is absent here.
units.anchor: use of AI by our students are already covered in our academic integrity policies

units.why: Names concerns with AI ('accuracy, potential biases, and privacy'), an informing statement about harms. P53 fits bias; it also touches accuracy and privacy, so a fit note is added.

units.fit_note: Asks users to consult review bodies before use; no specific approved tool list is named. | Directs consultation with unspecified institutional bodies before use rather than naming vetted tools.

documents.title: AI Research (Tulane student guidance on AI use)
documents.stance_why: The guide opens 'Tulane does not ban AI. Your instructor sets the rules for your course', and offers a cost-benefit ledger 'rather than a ban list'. No default allow or prohibit; the decision is delegated to the instructor, so delegates.
documents.summary: Library guide for students on using AI in research. It says Tulane does not ban AI, courses set the rules, and unauthorized generative AI breaches the Code of Academic Conduct, then sets out student duties to verify, disclose, protect data and weigh costs by research phase.

units.why: 'Disclose your use to instructors, editors, or reviewers' requires disclosure of AI use, P24.
units.anchor: Disclose your use to instructors, editors, or reviewers.

units.why: Warns of 'intellectual gaps' from depending on AI; a skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: Account for the intellectual gaps that come from depending on AI-generated content.
units.fit_note: An instruction to account for gaps rather than a claim that AI shortcuts practice.

units.why: Licensed content should be used 'only inside its native database's AI interface', a rule on which AI tools to use with library material, P92 (use approved tools).
units.anchor: use licensed library content only inside its native database's AI interface
units.fit_note: The approved environment is a vendor database's own AI, not a university-licensed tool. | Concerns the vendor's native AI interface for licensed content, not a university-wide approved list.

units.why: States a limitation of AI tools ('cannot reach resources behind paywalls'). No type covers tool capability limits beyond wrong output; P31 is the closest.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: actor=student, phase=during-work, modality=informs, policy_type=P31, unit_stance=neutral. Coder B: actor=student, phase=general, modality=informs, policy_type=P31, unit_stance=neutral. Resolution: Both: P31. A phase during-work, B general. Kept during-work: the reminder is among the points to keep in view while working with a generative tool. Final: actor=student, phase=during-work, modality=informs, policy_type=P31, unit_stance=neutral.
units.anchor: AI cannot reach resources behind paywalls or subscription databases.
units.fit_note: Describes a capability limit rather than errors in output. | A coverage limitation rather than wrong or hallucinated output.

units.why: 'you must acknowledge it' makes acknowledgment of permitted AI use mandatory, P24.
units.anchor: If your instructor permits AI use, you must acknowledge it.

units.why: Students 'Consult your instructor for their preferred style' of AI citation, pointing to instructor discretion and asking, P10 (ask) with delegation.
units.anchor: Consult your instructor for their preferred style.
units.fit_note: Asks about citation style, not about whether use is allowed. | Asks the instructor about citation style, not whether a use is allowed.

units.why: Distinguishes citation of specific output from a disclosure statement; 'most assignments that use AI need both'. P25 (cite the tool and output) fits because of the output-level citation; the sentence is a statement of fact about what assignments need, so informs.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: actor=student, phase=during-work, modality=should, policy_type=P25, unit_stance=neutral. Coder B: actor=student, phase=during-work, modality=informs, policy_type=P25, unit_stance=neutral. Resolution: Coder A modality should, B informs. 'most assignments that use AI need both' is a descriptive statement, not a directive (the directive 'you must acknowledge it' is a separate unit), so informs. Final: actor=student, phase=during-work, modality=informs, policy_type=P25, unit_stance=neutral.
units.anchor: most assignments that use AI need both
units.fit_note: Also requires a separate disclosure statement about how AI was used. | Distinguishes citation from disclosure without listing tool, prompt, or date.

notes: Reconciled from coder A and coder B. Course layer deferred; no school- or computing-level policy found. Provost letter and Faculty Guide not available. Dropped one B-only unit (Connolly Alexander Institute 'enhance data literacy across all disciplines'): it describes a data-science initiative, not AI use. Coder notes: A: Coder A. Provost letter and Faculty Guide not available, so the default stance rests on the two collected documents. The cost-benefit table in the LibGuide was coded only where it made policy-like statements. The data-protection rule appears in both documents and is coded in each. B: Only two university-layer documents included; the Provost's letter was not available. The library guide is a secondary source from an education library guide, so its scope is wider than computing.
